intro: Every excerpt below is copied from QI Hive's live source (the dashboard at C:\QIH\engine\hive, QI Brain at C:\QIH\engine\brain, the shared engine\common broker, the ecosystem registry, and the hive-* sub-agent definitions). QI Hive is the meta-platform that orchestrates the whole ecosystem, so this code is mostly glue, governance, and shared memory rather than a leaf product.

snippets.title: The dashboard app + CORS
snippets.feature: QI Hive Dashboard (port 8600) — the ecosystem control surface
snippets.code:
app = FastAPI(title="QI Hive", version="3.0.0")
app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory=str(Path(__file__).parent / "static")), name="static")
app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=["*"], allow_methods=["*"], allow_headers=["*"])
snippets.explanation: Creates the single FastAPI application that serves the whole dashboard on port 8600 (NSSM service QI_Dashboard). Static assets are mounted under /static and CORS is opened so any sibling QI service can call its JSON endpoints. Every route below hangs off this one app object.

snippets.title: Per-project status page route
snippets.feature: Project Status pages — the tabbed page you are reading right now
snippets.explanation: This is the route that renders this very page. It hands the project id and the selected tab to render_project_status() in project_status.py, which reads the INTRO/status_*.json + status_intro.md files and emits the Overview, Blueprint, Code Explained, Features, Tech Stack and Docs tabs.

snippets.title: Content-negotiated health probe
snippets.feature: Health endpoint that serves humans HTML and monitors JSON
snippets.explanation: One endpoint, two audiences. A browser (Accept: text/html) gets the rendered health dashboard; the QI validator and uptime monitors (default Accept or application/json) get a compact JSON probe. This closed the old 'health returns HTML not JSON' audit gap.

snippets.title: Block writes that arrive through the public tunnel
snippets.feature: Tunnel write-protection — public Cloudflare tunnel stays read-only without a token
snippets.explanation: Cloudflare injects cf-ray / cf-connecting-ip headers on tunnelled traffic. This middleware lets the public tunnel stay up for read access, but any mutating request (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) coming through it must carry the shared X-QI-Token, or it gets a 403. Direct localhost/LAN calls have neither header, so local workflow and hive agents are unaffected.

snippets.title: No-store on dynamic HTML
snippets.feature: Live pages never serve stale cache across origins
snippets.code:
@app.middleware("http")
async def no_store_html(request: Request, call_next):
    response = await call_next(request)
    ctype = response.headers.get("content-type", "")
    if ctype.startswith("text/html"):
        response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store, must-revalidate"
        response.headers["Pragma"] = "no-cache"
        response.headers["Expires"] = "0"
    return response
snippets.explanation: Dashboard pages render live on every request. This forces browsers to revalidate HTML so a public-tunnel origin can't show a stale launcher after services or tunnels change. Static assets keep their own caching since the guard only fires on text/html responses.

snippets.title: The single qi_brain.db connection helper
snippets.feature: One safe, WAL-mode gateway to the shared knowledge database
snippets.code:
DB_PATH = Path(os.environ.get("QI_BRAIN_DB", str(_DATA_DIR / "qi_brain.db")))

def open_brain_db(path: Path = DB_PATH) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    conn = sqlite3.connect(str(path), check_same_thread=False)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
    return conn
snippets.explanation: Every Brain module opens the database through this one helper so the PRAGMAs are always identical: WAL mode lets the API, poller, harvester and dashboard all touch C:\QIH\data\qi_brain.db concurrently; busy_timeout avoids 'database is locked' errors; foreign_keys keeps referential integrity across the 24 tables; Row factory gives column-name access.

snippets.title: The decisions table (governance memory)
snippets.feature: Permanent, supersede-able record of every architecture decision
snippets.code:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS decisions (
    decision_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    project_id       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(project_id),
    agent_id         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'claude' REFERENCES agents(agent_id),
    decision_code    TEXT UNIQUE,
    title            TEXT NOT NULL,
    rationale        TEXT NOT NULL,
    impact_scope     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'project',  -- 'project' | 'ecosystem' | 'global'
    tags             TEXT,
    superseded_by    INTEGER REFERENCES decisions(decision_id),
    superseded_at    TEXT,
    superseded_reason TEXT,
    recorded_at      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
);
snippets.explanation: The heart of QI's institutional memory (~491 rows). Each decision is tied to a project and the agent that logged it, scoped project/ecosystem/global, and is never deleted — it is superseded by pointing superseded_by at the newer decision. That is how get_context() can always surface the current ruling while keeping the audit trail.

snippets.title: Log a decision (SQL + vector in one call)
snippets.feature: qi.log_decision() — durable record plus semantic searchability
snippets.code:
@app.post("/api/log_decision")
async def log_decision(req: LogDecisionRequest):
    tags_json = json.dumps(req.tags or [])
    with open_brain_db() as conn:
        req.project_id = _resolve_pid(conn, req.project_id)
        cur = conn.execute(
            """INSERT INTO decisions
                (project_id, agent_id, decision_code, title, rationale, impact_scope, tags)
               VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)""",
            (req.project_id, req.agent_id, req.decision_code,
             req.title, req.rationale, req.impact_scope, tags_json))
        decision_id = cur.lastrowid
        conn.commit()
    # Embed into ChromaDB async
    text = f"{req.title}\n{req.rationale}"
    try:
        await _memory().add_decision(decision_id=decision_id, text=text,
            metadata={"project_id": req.project_id, "scope": req.impact_scope})
    except Exception:
        pass  # DB write succeeded; Chroma failure is non-fatal
    return {"ok": True, "decision_id": decision_id}
snippets.explanation: The dual-write that makes the Brain useful. The decision is committed to SQLite first (the source of truth), then vectorised into ChromaDB so it can be found by meaning later. If the embedding step fails the structured record still survives — Chroma is treated as a rebuildable index, not the primary store.

snippets.title: Budgeted session context assembly
snippets.feature: qi.get_context() — what a new session is told about the project
snippets.code:
decisions = conn.execute(
    """SELECT d.decision_id, d.decision_code, d.title, d.rationale,
              d.impact_scope, d.tags, d.project_id, d.recorded_at
       FROM decisions d
       WHERE d.superseded_by IS NULL
         AND (d.project_id = ? OR d.impact_scope IN ('ecosystem','global'))
         AND d.recorded_at >= ?
       ORDER BY
           CASE WHEN d.project_id = ? THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
           d.recorded_at DESC
       LIMIT 50""",
    (req.project_id, cutoff, req.project_id)).fetchall()

ranked_decisions = []
for row in decisions:
    d = dict(row)
    cost = _est_tokens(str(d))
    if used + cost > budget:
        break
    ranked_decisions.append(d)
    used += cost
snippets.explanation: When a session starts, this pulls only the still-current decisions (superseded_by IS NULL) for this project plus any ecosystem/global rulings, newest first, then packs them into the caller's token budget and stops once it is full. That is how a fresh Claude session is briefed without blowing the context window.

snippets.title: Four cosine-distance collections
snippets.feature: Vector memory: decisions, features, sessions and docs are all searchable by meaning
snippets.code:
COL_DECISIONS = "qi_decisions"
COL_FEATURES  = "qi_features"
COL_SESSIONS  = "qi_sessions"
COL_DOCS      = "qi_docs"
ALL_COLLECTIONS = [COL_DECISIONS, COL_FEATURES, COL_SESSIONS, COL_DOCS]

class MemoryStore:
    def __init__(self, chroma_path: Path = CHROMA_PATH):
        CHROMA_PATH.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self._client = chromadb.PersistentClient(
            path=str(chroma_path),
            settings=Settings(anonymized_telemetry=False))

    def _get_col(self, name: str):
        return self._client.get_or_create_collection(
            name=name, metadata={"hnsw:space": "cosine"})
snippets.explanation: The Brain's semantic layer. A persistent ChromaDB store at engine\brain\qi_memory holds four collections — decisions, features, session summaries and harvested ecosystem docs — each using cosine distance. Embeddings come from nomic-embed-text via the provider factory, so retrieval is by meaning rather than keyword.

snippets.title: Semantic search over a collection
snippets.feature: Find the closest records by meaning (powers the Documentation Brain search)
snippets.code:
async def search(self, query: str, collection: str = COL_DECISIONS,
                 n: int = 5, where: Optional[dict] = None) -> list[dict]:
    vec = await self._embed(query)
    col = self._get_col(collection)
    kwargs = {"query_embeddings": [vec], "n_results": n,
              "include": ["documents", "metadatas", "distances"]}
    if where:
        kwargs["where"] = where
    results = col.query(**kwargs)
    output = []
    for i, doc_id in enumerate(results["ids"][0]):
        output.append({"id": doc_id, "document": results["documents"][0][i],
                       "metadata": results["metadatas"][0][i],
                       "distance": results["distances"][0][i]})
    return output
snippets.explanation: Embeds the query with the same model used for storage, then asks ChromaDB for the n nearest vectors, returning each hit with its similarity distance. The dashboard's /api/library/search calls this (collection='docs') so a plain-English query finds the right doc across ~921 indexed files.

snippets.title: Never hardcode a port — derive CORS from the registry
snippets.feature: Single source of truth for ports / URLs across all 25 projects
snippets.explanation: The registry module any QI service imports. Instead of scattering port numbers and CORS origins across codebases, projects call QI.port('maia','api') or feed QI.cors_origins() straight into FastAPI — so changing a port is a one-line registry edit, not a hunt-and-replace. This enforces the ecosystem's 'no hardcoded values' law.

snippets.title: Port-block allocation rule
snippets.feature: Each project owns a dedicated port block — no random adjacent ports
snippets.explanation: The machine-readable governance that keeps services from colliding. Every family gets a reserved block; the validator and new-project wizard read this so a fresh service is assigned a port inside its own block rather than grabbing whatever is free. QI Brain sits at 9011 in the Hive block, the Dashboard at 8600.

snippets.title: Run a privileged command from a non-admin process
snippets.feature: QI_Elevate broker — restart services / run admin ops without UAC popups
snippets.code:
CMD_DIR = Path(r"C:\QIH\commands")
PENDING = CMD_DIR / "pending"
COMPLETED = CMD_DIR / "completed"

def run_elevated(cmd: str, args: list[str], submitted_by: str = "unknown",
                 timeout: float = 30.0, poll_interval: float = 0.5) -> dict:
    """Submit a command to the elevation broker and wait for the result."""
    rid = f"req_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')}_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}"
    request = {"id": rid, "cmd": cmd, "args": args,
               "submitted_by": submitted_by, "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat()}
    (PENDING / f"{rid}.json").write_text(json.dumps(request, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    result_path = COMPLETED / f"{rid}.json"
    deadline = time.time() + timeout
    while time.time() < deadline:
        if result_path.exists():
            return json.loads(result_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        time.sleep(poll_interval)
    raise TimeoutError(...)
snippets.explanation: The file-queue broker that replaced gsudo (which failed from headless contexts). A non-admin caller drops a request JSON in C:\QIH\commands\pending; the elevated QI_Elevate service picks it up, runs it, and writes the result to completed. The client just polls for that result — e.g. run_elevated('nssm', ['restart','QI_Dashboard']) restarts a service with no UAC prompt.

snippets.title: Scan committed source for leaked credentials
snippets.feature: Standards Enforcer — catches hardcoded tokens before they ship
snippets.code:
patterns = [
    (r'[0-9]{8,10}:AA[A-Za-z0-9_-]{30,}',  'Telegram bot token'),
    (r'sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}',          'Anthropic API key'),
    (r'sk-proj-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}',         'OpenAI API key'),
    (r'AIza[0-9A-Za-z_-]{30,}',             'Google API key'),
    (r'EAA[A-Za-z0-9]{60,}',                'Meta page/access token'),
    (r'gh[ops]_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}',           'GitHub token'),
]
hits = []
for pat, label in patterns:
    out = subprocess.run(
        ['git', '-C', str(path), 'grep', '-l', '-E', pat,
         '--', '*.py', '*.js', '*.json', '*.ps1', '*.md', '*.bat'],
        capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
    for f in out.stdout.split():
        hits.append(f"{label} in {f}")
if hits:
    did = file_dispatch(pid, 'secrets_in_source', msg, fix)
    return CheckResult('secrets_in_source', pid, 'fail', 'high', False, msg, fix, dispatch_id=did)
snippets.explanation: Added after live LINE/FB/Telegram tokens were found committed to maia_server.py. The inspector greps git-tracked files (so gitignored secrets are never flagged) for known credential shapes; any hit becomes a high-severity finding and is filed as a dispatch for follow-up. This is one of the checks the Inspector runs every 4 hours plus a nightly deep pass.

snippets.title: Detect unlogged work (Brain drift)
snippets.feature: Catches projects where code shipped but Brain never heard about it
snippets.explanation: Where check_session_freshness only notices silence, this notices unlogged activity: if the last git commit (or a session-summary .docx) is newer than the project's last session_log row in the Brain, work happened that the Brain never recorded. Added after an audit found project_state frozen and two projects entirely absent from the Brain.

snippets.title: A sub-agent is defined by Markdown front-matter
snippets.feature: Seven specialist hive agents loaded by Claude Code
snippets.code:
---
name: hive-architect
description: Strategic system designer for QI Hive. Use for architecture decisions, multi-project design, choosing patterns, breaking-change analysis, ADRs, and implementation plans before code is written. NOT for writing code — design only.
model: opus
tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, WebFetch, WebSearch
---

You are the **QI Hive Architect**. You design systems before anyone builds them.
snippets.explanation: Each hive agent is just a Markdown file: YAML front-matter declares its name, when to use it (description), which model it runs on, and which tools it may touch; the body is its system prompt. Claude Code loads every *.md in .claude\agents at startup. The architect runs on Opus and is read-only by design — it plans, it does not edit.

snippets.title: The dispatch discipline
snippets.feature: Agentic operating mode — main thread routes work to the right specialist
snippets.code:
### Workflow A — design + implement + ship
1. **hive-architect** (Opus) — design the change. Output: implementation plan.
2. **hive-builder** (Sonnet) — execute the plan. Output: code on disk.
3. **hive-inspector** (Sonnet) — review the change. Output: findings (pass / fail / fixes needed).
4. If inspector found issues: back to **hive-builder** with the findings.
5. **hive-scribe** (Haiku) — write session summary at end.
snippets.explanation: QI Hive's operating mode is a discipline, not magic: the main-thread Claude is the dispatcher and routes each sub-task to a specialist via Agent(subagent_type='hive-<role>'). The model assignment is deliberate cost control — Opus only for architecture, Sonnet for build/review, Haiku for cheap ops and docs — keeping delegation one level deep.

snippets.title: CoWork → Hive work-order endpoint
snippets.feature: External agents (CoWork) hand work to the Hive over HTTP
snippets.explanation: The integration seam between CoWork (Claude Work) and the Hive. Incoming work orders are typed: brain_update/decision/session payloads are forwarded to the Brain's inbox at :9011, while task_create drops a card onto the Hive board. This is how the 4-way architecture (CoWork / Claude Code / Hive / Renne) actually exchanges work.
